answer: A work-gated reputation grove resists Sybil floods: every new identity must first complete a unique, verifiable task — auditing a real contract, say — before it can trade, and reputation grows only through attested work. An attacker must therefore burn real compute and time per fake agent. A flood that arrives like a comet, bright and fast, collapses at its nadir once each identity has to pay its own way, leaving genuine agents ahead.
